differences.what: attribution of the large-dose design choice to a requirement from the source paper
differences.message_quote: with a per-layer dose of 6.76 (a large dose of the residual-norm order, as white-bear steering requires)
differences.writeup_quote: with a per-layer coefficient of 6.76 (a large dose, on the order of the residual norm there)

message_source_quote: This is distinct from Raman et al.'s *verbal* think/don't-think stance, and I established the visual-imagery contrast works where other stances fail.
writeup_source_quote: This extends white-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026), which showed a *verbal* think/don't-think stance works while hold-vs-mention does not.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering, frame the submitted method as building on/extending it rather than reproducing it, and identify the same novelty (a sensory-imagery contrast instead of a verbal one, plus the vividness/variety finding). The one added detail in the message — that the large dose is 'as white-bear steering requires' — slightly over-attributes a design parameter to the source paper's requirements, a nuance the write-up states only as an empirical observation without crediting it to the source's requirement.
